value_stream.name: Compact & Heavy Construction Equipment Rental Fleet Operations

fields.Frequency: Annual strategy refresh; ad-hoc expansion reviews
fields.Participants: VP Merchandising, CFO, COO, VP Store Operations, Supply Planning
fields.Trigger: Executive decision to enter/expand BuildRight-owned construction-equipment rental (beyond power tools and the W1094 brokerage model)
fields.Volume: 1 program strategy per year; ~1 category-mix decision per quarter

workflows.name: Compact & Heavy Equipment Rental Fleet Strategy, Category Mix & Business Case

Automation Opportunity: - Lost-sale/quote-to-demand pipeline: flag every B2B quote containing an equipment-rental need line and feed a rolling demand forecast per equipment class.
Controls: - CTL-02: prevent unauthorized capex — stage-gate approval; CTL-35 (budget adherence vs. approved envelope).
Cross-references: - links to VS-12.2 (tool rental), VS-40 (capex), VS-107 (key accounts), VS-11 (trade/project)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stranded-capex risk**: over-buying a fleet class that under-utilizes (e.g. a boom lift at a store with no high-rise trade base) erodes the ~60–70% utilization hurdle; mitigated by demand modeling from lost-sale and quote data and a hub-and-spoke rollout that concentrates high-value units at regional hubs with inter-store rebalancing (W5344).

- **Cannibalization risk**: pricing the fleet so low it cannibalizes the W1094 brokerage margin or VS-12.2 tool rental; mitigated by explicit rate-card separation and a documented value boundary in the strategy.
System Touchpoints: - ERP Fixed Asset / Rental Fleet module (asset class "Construction Equipment Rental"); capex request & approval workflow (VS-40 W1811).
Time Estimate: - ~4–6 weeks elapsed for the annual refresh; ~120 person-hours.

steps.activity: Quantify unmet demand from trade-account and project-quote data (lost sales where customer needed equipment BuildRight did not own — links VS-11/VS-107).
Build demand model by equipment class (earthmoving, concrete, access/lift, power/light/compressed-air, compaction) mapped to provincial construction activity and PHP/rental-day revenue.
Define category mix and store-tier fleet footprint (full-service vs. satellite vs. hub-and-spoke across 200 stores).
Build business case: capex (PHP 0.5M–8M/unit), utilization hurdle (~60–70%), payback, and attach uplift to material sales.
Present capex envelope and stage-gate to capital committee (per VS-40).

fields.Participants: Rental Fleet Manager, TESDA-qualified mechanic, Finance, Vendor (Komatsu/Kubota/Bobcat/JCB/Wacker Neuson/etc.)
fields.Volume: ~15–40 units per wave; ~60–120 units added/yr in steady state

workflows.name: Construction Equipment Vendor Selection, Procurement & Fleet Acquisition

Automation Opportunity: - Parts-availability and service-network data fed directly from OEM dealer portals into the RFP scorecard; auto-raise PO from approved wave list.
Controls: - CTL-06: vendor onboarding; CTL-14 (3-way match); CTL-26 (fixed asset capitalization control).
Cross-references: - links to VS-03 (vendor mgmt), VS-15 (P2P), VS-35 (fixed assets), VS-02.2 (inbound freight)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stranded-fleet risk**: buying a brand/model with no Philippines parts depot grounds units for weeks on a single failed hydraulic seal; mitigated by a mandatory local-parts-availability and dealer-service-network check in the RFP scoring, and a minimum 2-day spares kit on order at acquisition.

- **Spec-mismatch risk**: units arrive under-powered for PH jobsite conditions (e.g. a mini-excavator too heavy for typical residential slab access); mitigated by TESDA-qualified mechanic input in evaluation and a documented spec sheet per category.
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/PO module (VS-03/VS-15); Fixed Asset capitalization with rental-fleet asset class and serial/engine-number capture; 3-way match (PO→GR→invoice).

steps.activity: Issue RFP to equipment OEMs/dealers for rental-grade units with parts availability and after-sales support in the Philippines.
Evaluate on durability, hour-rating, local parts depots, dealer service network, and rental-program support (per W224 vendor selection).
Negotiate price, warranty, and fleet service agreement; confirm PHP landed cost including freight to DC (per VS-02.2).
Raise PO; receive units at the assigned hub DC; inspect against spec and register assets (W5324).
Acceptance sign-off and asset capitalization to the Rental Fleet GL class.

fields.Frequency: Per hub/satellite setup (~10–20 sites/yr as the network rolls out)
fields.Participants: Store Manager, HSE Officer, BFP-accredited Fire Safety Inspector, Corporate Security (VS-159)
fields.Trigger: New hub store selected for an equipment-rental footprint (W5321)

workflows.name: Rental Equipment Yard, Wash Bay & Heavy-Equipment Storage Infrastructure Setup

Automation Opportunity: - Yard-design template and BOM auto-generated per tier (hub/satellite) from the approved footprint.
Controls: - CTL-104: rental-fleet asset safeguarding at the yard; operational: BFP FSIC sign-off before commissioning.
Cross-references: - links to VS-20 (construction), VS-138 (facilities), VS-166 (permits), VS-24 (HSE), VS-159 (security)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Environmental liability risk**: equipment wash-down runoff (oil, hydraulic fluid, concrete slurry) discharged without an interceptor triggers DENR-EMB violation under RA 9275 (Clean Water Act); mitigated by an oil-water interceptor + sump and a quarterly effluent check.

- **Theft risk**: high-value capital equipment (a PHP 5M boom lift) parked in an inadequately lit/fenced yard is a prime target; mitigated by fenced/lighted/CCTV yard design and telematics kill-switch (W5324).
System Touchpoints: - Facilities/CAPEX project module; BFP FSIC and DENR-ECC permit records (links VS-166 permit portfolio).
Time Estimate: - ~6–8 weeks elapsed per yard; capital project, ~PHP 2–6M per site.

steps.activity: Design the rental yard: compacted/graded laydown, security lighting, CCTV coverage, fenced perimeter, and equipment-tier separation.
Build wash-down bay with oil-water interceptor and sump (DENR-ECC compliant for wash runoff, per VS-24/VS-187).
Install fueling/battery-charge station, spill kit, and fire suppression rated for diesel/equipment (BFP Fire Code FSIC).
Commission the yard; sign off HSE and BFP FSIC before first unit intake.

workflows.name: Heavy Equipment Rental Fleet Asset Registration, Tracking & Telematics Provisioning

Automation Opportunity: - Telematics feed auto-populates the rental asset's hour-meter and location, eliminating manual readings; geofence breach auto-creates a recovery ticket.
Controls: - CTL-219: rental-fleet asset registration; operational: dual-control telematics-provisioning sign-off (IT + Mechanic).
Cross-references: - links to VS-35 (fixed assets), VS-27 (IoT/IT ops), VS-99 (technology lifecycle)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Invisible-fleet risk**: a unit without telematics is "lost" the moment it leaves the yard — no usage billing accuracy, no theft recovery; mitigated by mandatory telematics provisioning before first rental and a kill-switch on units > PHP 1M.

- **Hour-meter drift risk**: maintenance scheduled on hour-meter readings that the telematics under-reports causes missed PM and in-field breakdowns; mitigated by daily hour-meter-feed health checks and variance alerts.
System Touchpoints: - Rental Fleet asset master (per-unit serial/hour-meter); telematics/IoT platform ingesting GPS + hour-meter + geofence events into ERP; Fixed Asset register.

steps.activity: Capture unit identity: OEM, model, serial, engine number, hour-meter baseline, photos, and any VIN/registration.
Install telematics/IoT unit (GPS, hour-meter feed, geofence, kill-switch where fitted).
Register the unit in the Rental Fleet module as a unique rentable asset with utilization/maintenance counters.
Link telematics feed to the ERP rental-lifecycle events (pickup, return, geofence breach).
Capitalize asset and reconcile to the PO/invoice (per VS-35).

fields.Frequency: Quarterly rate review; ad-hoc per competitor move
fields.Participants: COO, Finance Business Partner, Competitive Intelligence (VS-57)
fields.Trigger: Fleet intake (W5322) and quarterly margin review
fields.Volume: 1 rate card per quarter covering ~25–40 equipment classes

workflows.name: Equipment Rental Rate Card, Pricing Structure & Competitor Benchmarking

Automation Opportunity: - Competitor-rate scraping (VS-57) feeds directly into the rate-build workbook; rate-card changes propagate to POS and the booking channel in one publish.
Controls: - CTL-07: prevent unauthorized pricing changes — rate-card change approval; CTL-35 (margin adherence).
Cross-references: - links to VS-57 (competitive price intelligence), VS-118 (revenue assurance/pricing integrity)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-recovery risk**: a daily rate that does not cover capex amortization at the realized utilization bleeds margin silently; mitigated by a per-class break-even utilization model in the rate build and weekly realized-rate monitoring.
- **Price-leadership risk**: undercutting the brokerage (W1094) channel or being uncompetitive vs. specialty rental houses; mitigated by competitor benchmarking and a documented positioning band.
System Touchpoints: - Rental pricing/rate-card module (per-class hourly/daily/weekly); POS rental pricing; competitive-price-intel feed (VS-57).
Time Estimate: - ~2 weeks per quarterly review; ~10 person-hours/week ongoing monitoring.

steps.activity: Gather competitor rental rates (specialty rental houses, peer big-box) by class and region.
Build hourly/daily/weekly/monthly rate per class covering capex amortization, utilization, fuel/wear, and target margin.
Define CDW (collision damage waiver) fee, delivery fee, and late/overtime rate.
Load rate card to POS/rental module; publish to the digital booking channel (W5328).
Monitor realized rate vs. rate card weekly and flag erosion.

fields.Participants: Credit Analyst (VS-68), HSE Officer, Compliance Specialist
fields.Trigger: New customer applies for self-operated equipment rental; periodic re-qualification
fields.Volume: ~3,000–6,000 first-time renters/yr; ~15,000 active renters in the base

workflows.name: Rental Operator Certification, Customer Pre-Qualification & Credit/License Vetting

Automation Opportunity: - Online pre-qualification with ID upload and credit-card pre-auth that opens/holds the rental account before the customer reaches the counter.
Controls: - CTL-12: separate credit approval from sales execution — counter staff cannot override a credit reject; CTL-27 (customer data safeguards on the captured IDs).
Cross-references: - links to VS-68 (credit risk), VS-16 (order-to-cash), VS-86 (AML/KYC), VS-167 (background screening)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Negligent-rental risk**: renting an aerial lift or mini-excavator to an untrained operator who injures a third party exposes BuildRight to liability and DOLE findings; mitigated by mandatory competency check or signed operator-acknowledgment (W5330 safety briefing) and CDW/insurance (W5327).
- **Credit-loss risk**: a renter absconds with a PHP 5M unit on a weak credit check; mitigated by credit-card pre-auth / trade-account standing and deposit hold sized to the unit value.
System Touchpoints: - Rental customer master + credit-hold integration (VS-68/VS-16); document vault (VS-88); sanctions/PEP check (VS-86) for large deposits.

steps.activity: Capture renter identity, valid government ID, and (for B2B) PCAB license and business registration.
Run credit check / credit-card pre-auth / trade-account standing (links VS-68/VS-16).
Verify operator competency: valid license/TCO where the class requires it (e.g. heavy-vehicle-restricted units), or issue an in-store competency check + signed acknowledgment.
Capture and store the signed rental agreement, CDW election, and operator certification in the rental customer record (VS-88).
Flag any reject (failed credit, no competency, sanctioned party) and prevent rental-lifecycle start.

fields.Frequency: Annual policy renewal; per-unit endorsement on intake
fields.Trigger: Fleet intake (W5322) and annual insurance renewal
fields.Volume: 1 master policy/yr covering the fleet; ~60–120 unit endorsements/yr

workflows.name: Heavy Equipment Insurance, Collision Damage Waiver (CDW) & Liability Program Setup

Automation Opportunity: - Per-rental CDW election auto-posted to the policy/claims register and to the captive ledger.
Controls: - CTL-104: rental-fleet insurance & damage-recovery coverage; operational: default-on CDW with documented opt-out.
Cross-references: - links to VS-26 (insurance), VS-153 (captive), VS-100 (legal), VS-159 (security/investigations)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Uninsured-loss risk**: a unit rented without CDW/elected coverage and damaged off-site leaves BuildRight to absorb the full repair; mitigated by a default-on CDW (opt-out only) or mandatory deposit sized to the deductible.
- **Mis-priced-CDW risk**: a CDW fee that does not cover the actuarial first-loss erodes margin; mitigated by annual loss-ratio review against the CDW revenue pool.
System Touchpoints: - Insurance policy/claims register (links VS-26); rental POS CDW election; captive underwriting ledger (VS-153).

steps.activity: Define coverage: physical damage (comprehensive), third-party liability, and hired/borrowed operator coverage, sized to unit values (PHP 0.5M–8M).
Structure CDW as an optional customer fee that shifts the deductible/first-loss to the renter (per RA 10607 non-life insurance rules / the captive).
Negotiate master policy + premiums with broker/insurer; consider captive participation (VS-153) for the predictable first-loss layer.
Configure per-rental CDW election and deductible into the rental rate card (W5325) and POS.
Establish claims protocol linking to incident management (W5341) and recovery (W5334).

fields.Frequency: Per intake wave; ongoing availability sync

workflows.name: Equipment Rental Catalog, Merchandising & Digital Booking Channel Integration

Automation Opportunity: - Real-time availability from the rental-asset ledger published to all booking channels; automated "frequently rented together" merchandising.
Controls: - CTL-788 (ensure controlled execution — Fleet Strategy, Acquisition & Yard Infrastructure (PA-186.1).)
- operational: any operator-license/ID data captured online is safeguarded; operational: PIM content review before publish.
Cross-references: - links to VS-137 (PIM/DAM), VS-10 (ecommerce), VS-14 (marketing), VS-60 (omnichannel)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-information risk**: an outdated load rating or omitted operator-license requirement in the catalog causes a wrong rental and a safety/return dispute; mitigated by PIM governance and a mandatory operator-requirement field per class.
- **Double-booking risk**: a unit booked online and rented in-store simultaneously; mitigated by real-time availability sync to a single rental-asset ledger (not a channel-local copy).
System Touchpoints: - PIM/DAM (VS-137); ecommerce/web/app booking (VS-10); rental availability/reservation module; omnichannel inventory sync (VS-60).
Time Estimate: - ~2 hours/class for content; ~3 weeks for initial channel integration; ongoing sync automated.

steps.activity: Author rental product content per class: specs, load/capacity ratings, photos, operator requirements, and safety video (per VS-137 PIM/DAM).
Publish to web/app booking channel with real-time availability by store/hub (links VS-10).
Merchandise in-store: yard signage, "Rent It" shelf-edge tags on merchandise that pairs with equipment (e.g. a breaker hammer near the jackhammer rental).
Integrate online booking → rental reservation → counter handover workflow (W5329).
Sync availability across channels to prevent double-booking (links VS-60 omnichannel).
